commit_message:
[wasm] Support inlining Proxy-on-Prototype traps

When a Wasm object's prototype chain is sufficiently immutable,
we can statically retrieve Proxy traps on it and embed them as
constants. The existing Wasm-into-JS inlining support can then
even inline the calls, making keyed load/store accesses from
optimized code via these Proxy traps much faster.

Bug: 403372470

findings.title: Missing IC kind guard in FeedbackNexus::IsOneMapManyNames() causes DCHECK crash for KeyedHasIC
findings.message: FeedbackNexus::IsOneMapManyNames() does not check the IC kind before classifying feedback as the '1 map, many names' type. This type is only valid for keyed load/store ICs, but the function can return true for KeyedHasIC feedback when the slot holds a Wasm object map with a generic handler. Commit ef9dafb5ab5 changed js-heap-broker.cc to call ProcessFeedbackMapsForKeyedPropertyAccess() whenever IsOneMapManyNames() returns true; that function contains DCHECK(keyed_mode.string_keys()). For KeyedHasIC, KeyedAccessMode::FromNexus() hard-codes string_keys=false (kStringKeysUnsupported), so the DCHECK fires and V8 crashes in debug builds.
findings.suggestion: Add an IC kind guard at the top of IsOneMapManyNames() to return false immediately for any IC that is not a keyed load or keyed store IC, since the '1 map, many names' feedback state is only produced by those two IC kinds.

ground_truth.root_cause: IsOneMapManyNames() checks only the shape of the feedback slot (a weak map reference + a Smi matching LoadGeneric/StoreGeneric) without first verifying that the FeedbackSlotKind is actually a keyed load or store IC. The '1 map, many names' mode is exclusively used by keyed load/store ICs; applying the same classification logic to KeyedHasIC feedback produces a false positive that subsequently violates the invariant asserted by ProcessFeedbackMapsForKeyedPropertyAccess.
